heading: Maximising Savings: 9 Reinvestment Options for Capital Gains Tax Exemption
tldr: Selling capital assets like property, land, shares, or mutual funds can lead to capital gains tax.
The Income-tax Act, 1961, offers exemptions if these gains are reinvested in specific assets.
Sections 54, 54F, and 54EC are commonly used for reinvesting in residential property or specified bonds.
There are nine distinct sections allowing exemptions, each with specific conditions and timelines.
Understanding these options can significantly reduce your tax liability when selling assets.
caption:
Sold a property or some shares recently? You might be wondering about the tax on your profit. Good news! The government lets you save on this tax if you reinvest that profit wisely. Our new article explains nine simple ways to do this, from buying another home to investing in special bonds. It’s all about keeping more of your hard-earned money. Learn how to make the most of your capital gains – read the full article now.
